required_sections.name: NeurIPS Paper Checklist
required_sections.requirement: mandatory
required_sections.placement: inside the PDF after references (and after optional appendices)
required_sections.note: Papers without the checklist were desk-rejected in 2025; same treatment assumed for 2026.

required_sections.name: Limitations
required_sections.requirement: strongly encouraged (checklist item 2 recommends a separate section; reviewers are told not to penalize honest limitations)

required_sections.name: Broader impacts
required_sections.requirement: addressed through checklist item 10 (discuss positive and negative impacts or justify NA)

required_sections.name: Declaration of LLM usage
required_sections.requirement: only when the LLM is a core-method component that is 'important, original, or non-standard' (checklist item 16); writing/editing/formatting-only use is exempt

required_sections.name: Safeguards, asset licenses, new-asset documentation, human-subject details, IRB
required_sections.requirement: when applicable (checklist items 11-15)

checklist.question: Do the main claims in the abstract and introduction correctly reflect what the paper contributes and the scope of that contribution?
Does the paper acknowledge and discuss where its own approach and results fall short?
For every theoretical result, are all assumptions stated and is a complete and correct proof provided?
Is all information needed to reproduce the main experimental results (to the extent they affect the main claims or conclusions) disclosed, whether or not code and data are released?

checklist.short_name: Open access to data and code
checklist.question: Are data and code openly provided, with instructions in the supplementary material sufficient to faithfully reproduce the main results?

Does the paper give every training and evaluation detail needed to make sense of the results, such as how the data were split, which hyperparameters were used and how they were picked, and the optimizer?
Are suitably and correctly defined error bars, or other appropriate statistical-significance information, reported for the experiments?
For each experiment, is there enough information on the compute used (type of workers, memory, execution time) to reproduce it?
Does the research conform in every respect to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics?
Does the paper discuss both potential positive and potential negative societal impacts of the work?
Are safeguards described for the responsible release of data or models with high misuse risk (e.g., pretrained language models, image generators, scraped datasets)?
Are the creators or original owners of used assets (code, data, models) properly credited, and are their licenses and terms of use stated and respected?
Are new assets introduced by the paper well documented, with the documentation supplied alongside them?

checklist.short_name: Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects
checklist.question: For crowdsourcing or human-subject research, does the paper give the full participant instructions, screenshots where applicable, and compensation details?

checklist.short_name: Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects
checklist.question: Does the paper describe risks to participants, whether those risks were disclosed to them, and whether IRB (or equivalent) approval was obtained?
Is LLM use described whenever an LLM is a core-method component that is 'important, original, or non-standard'? Use limited to writing, editing or formatting is exempt.

venues.checklist_answer_format: Each item: Answer [Yes] / [No] / [N/A] plus a short Justification (ideally pointing to sections). [No] or [N/A] on Claims or Reproducibility 'will not be perceived well'; [No] is acceptable for open code/data unless code is central (e.g., a benchmark).
venues.supplementary: Optional technical appendices may follow the references in the main PDF (no page limit; reviewers are not obliged to read them; locked at the full-paper deadline). Code/data may go in a separate ZIP (100 MB cap in 2025; 2026 cap unverified). All supplementary material was due with the full paper on 2026-05-06.
venues.dual_submission_and_arxiv: Governed by the Main Track Handbook. A third-party paper quoting the handbook reports that archival submissions by an overlapping author set are treated as prior work, thin-slicing is prohibited, and submitting the same paper to the main and E&D tracks counts as dual submission; papers cannot be moved between tracks or contribution types. Dual submission to non-archival workshops is allowed. arXiv posting rules for 2026 not verified (allowed in earlier editions).
venues.llm_policy: Only humans can be authors (2025 policy; the 2026 E&D guidelines also say agents/LLMs cannot be authors). Authors must document important, original or non-standard use of LLMs/agents in the methodology (handbook section 'Author Use of Agents and Large Language Models'). Prompt injection aimed at reviewers is strictly prohibited. The Position Paper track has a stricter 'substantially human-written' rule.
other_rules: Select exactly one contribution type at submission; the review form is shared but criteria are interpreted per type (Concept & Feasibility and Negative Results carry a higher significance/originality bar).
Reviewer criteria: Quality (technical soundness), Clarity (relative to an ML audience), Significance, Originality (evaluating existing methods for new insight can count).
Main track ran a sanctioned LLM-support experiment for reviewers via OpenReview; low-quality reviews may be checked for inappropriate LLM use.
Position Paper track: no checklist required.

rules.rule: Answer every substantive reviewer point, starting with concerns shared by several reviewers or most likely to change the decision; draft answers to everything first, then prioritize and trim.

Writing advice from Karpathy, Jia-Bin Huang and Eisner was read in full (GitHub copies / mirror); Peyton Jones, Widom, Lipton & Steinhardt, Gopen & Swan, McEnerney, Pinker, Black, Freeman, Fatahalian and Parikh/Batra/Lee via search summaries; Kording & Mensh, Mermin and Knuth et al. from prior knowledge (flagged as such).
